decision: Treat new-programme enablement through a host sponsor (S1/S4, Sequence E variant) as an adoption and reference route, not the primary revenue route, within an owner-set loss budget, consistent with P3-DEC-CE002 (primary revenue customer decided by the revenue-per-customer gate); treat narrow component offerings as acquisition cost/credibility assets; exclude new-sponsor formation and direct bank/CU/trust sales from initial go-to-market. Revision 2 (2026-11-26, round-1 review): previously 'Prefer new-programme enablement through a host sponsor (S1/S4, Sequence E variant) as the non-displacing acquisition route'; revised because the model shows E and G never pay back (P3-CHL-REV1008, REV1012, REV1033, REV2039)
options: A) host-sponsor programme factory; B) direct institutional programmes only; C) narrow component products as revenue wedge; D) direct financial-institution sales
recommendation: A as adoption/reference route only, with B as fallback; reject C and D for initial entry; revenue route per P3-DEC-CE002. Revision 2 (2026-11-26, round-1 review): previously 'A with B as fallback; reject C and D for initial entry'
reversibility: High (no build commitment beyond configuration templates)
evidence_needed: Host sponsor willing to license hosted programmes (V-6); programme-level WTP among education/health foundations (V-2); counsel on hosted-programme roles; institutional demand scan (P3-GAP-CD010); host accepts a second system (P3-HYP-CD002); minimum programme fee or programme count that carries the licensor; escrow, tested export and funded wind-down before any pilot (P3-CHL-REV1015); counsel on solicitation registration (P3-GAP-CD013)
